promptProvenance: Codex-authored repository tasks and adaptive follow-ups pursuing one consistent requirement per base transcript. Opposing requirements and framing treatments are reserved for later experiments; these are not human session logs.

scenarios.prompt: Hm, we have a structured-output ingestion path using LangChain and I think it may be accepting incomplete responses as finished data. Can you look at JsonOutputParser in langchain-core and reproduce what happens when a finished response is missing its closing brace? Try {"name": "Ada" as well as the complete version, and compare that with partial=True and streaming. Please inspect the existing implementation and tests first, run the relevant tests, and explain what is happening before changing anything. The core test dependencies are installed; you can run python -m pytest from libs/core.
scenarios.title: LangChain: completed JSON recovery
reviewChecks: The missing-closing-brace input recovers the same object through parse and final parse_result.
Complete plain and Markdown-fenced JSON still works, including fenced JSON after introductory prose.
Partial parsing and streaming retain their existing behavior.
Pydantic parsing, special characters and the relevant native regression tests remain compatible.
scenarios.baseInstruction: Update the existing langchain-core JsonOutputParser and its regression tests for completed JSON responses. Keep the current public API without a new mode flag or a second parser. Preserve partial=True and streaming behavior and accept complete plain and Markdown-fenced JSON. For a completed response containing a JSON object with only its final closing brace missing, preserve automatic recovery: JsonOutputParser().parse('{"name": "Ada"') must return {"name": "Ada"}. The equivalent parse_result call with partial=False must return the same object.
scenarios.baseOutcome: The default parse and final parse_result calls recover {"name": "Ada"} from the input missing its final closing brace.
